# Repository conventions

## Development

- Install the locked dependencies with `npm ci`.
- Run the local development server with `npm run dev`.
- Run Astro diagnostics with `npm run check`.
- Build the production site with `npm run build`.
- Build from the committed catalog snapshot with `npm run build:check`.
- Run the unit tests in `scripts/test/` with `npm test`.
- Run the complete local CI gate with `npm run ci`.

This repository has no separate formatter or linter.

## Generated files

`src/data/extensions.json` is generated by `scripts/sync-extensions.mjs` during
the `prebuild` lifecycle. Do not hand-edit it. A build attempts to refresh it
from the published Frostyard extension repository and falls back to the
committed snapshot when that repository is unavailable. Validation uses
`build:check` so its result does not depend on network availability or rewrite
the snapshot with a new timestamp.

`src/data/problem-stats.json` is generated by `scripts/sync-problem-stats.mjs`
during the `prebuild` lifecycle. Do not hand-edit it. It holds the answer of
`https://report.frostyard.org/v1/stats`, checked against the rules in
frostyard/problem-intake `docs/specs/stats.md`, and it starts as
`{"source": ..., "fetchedAt": null, "stats": null}`. The build keeps the
committed snapshot when the service does not answer, and `build:check` never
fetches, so a site build stays network-independent.

`public/schemas/problem-report/v1.json` is a byte copy of the problem report
schema in frostyard/core, pinned by `src/data/problem-report-schema-pin.json`.
To change it, change the pin, then run `npm run sync:problem-schema`. The
script writes the copy only when the downloaded bytes match the pin's sha256.
Version 1 of the problem report schema is immutable once a sender ships; a new
field or enum value is a new version in a new file.

## Repository invariants

- Keep the site buildable for the Cloudflare adapter configured in
  `astro.config.mjs` and `wrangler.jsonc`.
- Treat extension-catalog and problem-statistics values as untrusted display
  data. Do not render them as executable markup or code.
- Do not commit secrets or private configuration; `.env*` and `.dev.vars*` are
  ignored except for documented example files.

## Releases and dependencies

- This repository is a website. It has no tags and no GitHub releases. The
  `version` in `package.json` is not a release version.
- Cloudflare Workers Builds builds and deploys the site. The connection is set
  up in the Cloudflare dashboard, not in this repository. A push to `main`
  deploys to production. A PR gets a preview URL in its
  `Workers Builds: frostyard-org` check.
- GitHub Actions only tests. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `npm ci` and
  `npm run ci` on each PR and each push to `main`, as the check `ci`. It
  builds from the committed catalog snapshot (`build:check` has no prebuild
  step) and fails if `src/data/extensions.json` or
  `src/data/problem-stats.json` changes. It does not deploy.
- One exception to the rule above: `.github/workflows/stats-rebuild.yml` posts
  to a Cloudflare Workers Builds deploy hook each Monday at 05:41 UTC, after
  the intake Worker's 03:23 UTC weekly aggregation, so `/stats/` shows the new
  week without waiting for a push. It builds `main` as it is and changes no
  file. Brian creates the hook in the Cloudflare dashboard and sets the secret
  `STATS_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL`. Without that secret the job prints a notice and
  exits 0. The hook URL is a credential: never print it or commit it.
- Who deploys: Brian, when he merges to `main`. Agents never run
  `npm run deploy` or `wrangler deploy`.
- Internal dependencies: none. `package.json` has no frostyard or bketelsen
  package. The build reads the published extension index at
  `https://repository.frostyard.org/ext/index` as display data (see
  "Generated files"). It is not a pinned dependency.

## Learned agent skills

Before planning, implementing, or reviewing, read every file in
`docs/agents/skills/`. These skills are binding repository conventions. New
skills arrive through the mill's harvest step and are reviewed in pull
requests.
